newsitem.title: UK: LVMH chief votes against GrandMet/Guinness merger.
newsitem.headline: LVMH chief votes against GrandMet/Guinness merger.

text.p: Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods and drinks group LVMH Moet Hennessy and a non-executive director of Guinness, voted against the proposed merger of Grand Metropolitan and Guinness.
Arnault voted against the merger at a meeting of the Guinness board on May 9, expressing reservations about its rationale, GrandMet and Guinness said in a joint statement.
LVMH has a shareholding of 14.2 percent in Guinness and under an existing agreement LVMH has agreed not to buy any further Guinness shares beyond the level of 15 percent.

"He (Arnault) has also written to the chairmen of GrandMet and Guinness suggesting discussions of a possible transaction which would involve a combination of the three spirits and wines businesses of GrandMet, Guinness and Moet Hennessy as an independent listed group," said the statement.

Guinness and LVMH have promised not to engage in any champagne or cognac activities that compete with Moet Hennessy's, so the merger of GrandMet and Guinness will require the sale of champagne and cognac businesses.

The boards of Guinness and GrandMet have told Arnault they think their shareholders will enjoy higher growth and shareholder value through a merger than through spinning off a single spirits business, said the statement.
